available_detectors.name: IForest
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n * t * log(n)) where t is n_estimators
strengths: Linear time complexity with efficient implementation
Does not require distance or density computation
weaknesses: May struggle with local anomalies in dense regions
Axis-aligned splits can miss anomalies in correlated features
available_detectors.best_for: General-purpose anomaly detection especially on large or high-dimensional datasets
available_detectors.avoid_when: Anomalies are local density deviations or features are strongly correlated

available_detectors.name: KNN
weaknesses: Sensitive to distance metric and k choice
available_detectors.best_for: General-purpose distance-based outlier detection on moderate-sized datasets
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large or has highly variable local densities

available_detectors.name: ECOD
strengths: Strong benchmark performance across diverse datasets
weaknesses: May struggle with strongly correlated features
Assumes outliers deviate in at least one marginal dimension
available_detectors.best_for: General-purpose outlier detection when speed and interpretability are priorities
available_detectors.avoid_when: Features are heavily correlated and outliers only manifest in joint distributions

available_detectors.name: COPOD
strengths: Models tail probabilities via empirical copulas
weaknesses: Assumes feature-wise independence for tail modeling
available_detectors.best_for: Large-scale datasets where speed and interpretability matter and features are roughly independent
available_detectors.avoid_when: Outliers only appear in joint distributions with strong feature dependencies

available_detectors.name: HBOS
available_detectors.best_for: Large-scale datasets where speed is critical and features are roughly independent
available_detectors.avoid_when: Outliers only manifest through feature interactions or correlations

available_detectors.name: ABOD
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n^2 * d) for fast, O(n^3 * d) for default
strengths: Not affected by distance concentration in high dimensions
weaknesses: Computationally expensive, especially in default mode
Sensitive to noise in low-dimensional data
Requires sufficient neighbors for angle variance estimation
available_detectors.best_for: High-dimensional datasets where distance-based methods suffer from curse of dimensionality
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large or low-dimensional where distance-based methods work well

available_detectors.name: AE1SVM
strengths: Jointly optimizes autoencoder and one-class SVM
Combines representation learning with boundary detection
weaknesses: Requires tuning of both AE and SVM hyperparameters
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets benefiting from joint representation learning and one-class classification
available_detectors.avoid_when: Simpler pipeline of separate AE + SVM works well, or dataset is small

available_detectors.name: ALAD
strengths: Bi-directional GAN avoids slow iterative inference of AnoGAN
weaknesses: Still subject to GAN training challenges
available_detectors.best_for: Scenarios where GAN-based detection is desired but fast inference is needed
available_detectors.avoid_when: Simpler reconstruction-based deep methods suffice or dataset is small

available_detectors.name: AnoGAN
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n * d * h * epochs) + O(n * iterations) for inference
strengths: GAN learns the normal data distribution
Anomaly scoring via reconstruction in latent space
weaknesses: Slow inference due to iterative latent optimization
available_detectors.best_for: Complex data distributions where GAN-based generation quality is high
available_detectors.avoid_when: Fast inference is needed or training instability is a concern

available_detectors.name: AutoEncoder
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n * d * h * epochs) where h is hidden size
strengths: Reconstruction error is an intuitive anomaly score
weaknesses: Requires tuning of architecture and hyperparameters
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets with complex nonlinear structure where reconstruction-based scoring is appropriate
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is small, tabular and simple methods suffice, or training time is limited

available_detectors.name: CBLOF
strengths: Combines clustering with local outlier scoring
Effective when data has clear cluster structure
weaknesses: Depends on quality of underlying clustering
Sensitive to number of clusters parameter
May fail if data does not cluster well
available_detectors.best_for: Data with well-separated clusters where outliers deviate from cluster structure
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data has no meaningful cluster structure or clusters are heavily overlapping

available_detectors.name: CD
strengths: Based on classical influence measures from regression
Interpretable as influence on regression fit
Works well when a regression model is appropriate
weaknesses: Not suitable for purely unsupervised settings without a model
available_detectors.best_for: Identifying influential observations in regression settings
available_detectors.avoid_when: No natural target variable exists or data is purely unsupervised

available_detectors.name: COF
strengths: Better than LOF for certain pattern structures
Handles low-density patterns in neighborhood chains
weaknesses: Marginal improvement over LOF in many cases
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets where outliers lie along sparse connectivity paths between clusters
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is large or simpler methods like LOF already perform well

available_detectors.name: DIF
strengths: Uses deep random representations for better isolation
Extends isolation forest to representation space
weaknesses: More computationally expensive than standard IForest
available_detectors.best_for: Complex datasets where standard Isolation Forest misses anomalies due to axis-aligned splits
available_detectors.avoid_when: Standard Isolation Forest performs well or dataset is small and simple

available_detectors.name: DeepSVDD
strengths: Learns a compact hypersphere around normal data
Combines deep learning with SVDD objective
available_detectors.best_for: One-class anomaly detection where a compact normal data description is desired
available_detectors.avoid_when: Normal data is multi-modal or simpler one-class methods are sufficient

available_detectors.name: DevNet
strengths: Can leverage a few labeled anomalies (semi-supervised)
Deviation loss directly optimizes anomaly scores
weaknesses: Requires at least a few labeled anomalies for best results
Sensitive to architecture and loss parameters
available_detectors.best_for: Semi-supervised anomaly detection where a small number of labeled anomalies are available
available_detectors.avoid_when: No labeled anomalies are available or dataset is too small for deep learning

available_detectors.name: FeatureBagging
weaknesses: Performance depends on choice of base detector
Slower than single detector due to ensemble overhead
May not improve over base if features are all relevant
available_detectors.best_for: High-dimensional data with potentially irrelevant features
available_detectors.avoid_when: All features are relevant or a single strong detector suffices

available_detectors.name: GMM
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n * k * d^2) per EM iteration
weaknesses: Sensitive to initialization and number of components
EM convergence not guaranteed to global optimum
available_detectors.best_for: Data with multi-modal distributions that can be approximated by Gaussian mixtures
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data does not follow mixture-of-Gaussians assumption or is very high-dimensional

available_detectors.name: HDBSCAN
strengths: Automatically finds clusters of varying density
Identifies noise points as potential outliers
weaknesses: May be slow for very large datasets
Outlier scores derived from cluster membership
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets with variable-density clusters where noise points are outliers
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data does not have cluster structure or very high-dimensional

available_detectors.name: INNE
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n * t * s) where t is n_estimators, s is sample size
strengths: Handles local anomalies better than Isolation Forest
weaknesses: Requires tuning of sample size and number of estimators
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets where local density variations matter and Isolation Forest underperforms
available_detectors.avoid_when: A simpler method like IForest already works well

available_detectors.name: KDE
weaknesses: Sensitive to bandwidth and kernel selection
available_detectors.best_for: Low-to-moderate dimensional data where non-parametric density estimation is desired
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data is high-dimensional or dataset is very large

available_detectors.name: KPCA
strengths: Captures nonlinear relationships via kernel trick
Extension of PCA to nonlinear manifolds
available_detectors.best_for: Moderately sized datasets with nonlinear structure
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large due to quadratic kernel matrix or a linear model suffices

available_detectors.name: LMDD
strengths: Multiple deviation measures available (AAD, IQR, MAD)
weaknesses: Results can vary due to random projections
Requires tuning of number of iterations and measure
May underperform with nonlinear anomaly patterns
available_detectors.best_for: Multivariate data where anomalies are detectable through linear projections
available_detectors.avoid_when: Anomalies require nonlinear feature combinations to detect

available_detectors.name: LOCI
strengths: Multi-granularity outlier detection via alpha parameter
Does not require explicit k-neighbor parameter
weaknesses: Difficult to scale to large datasets
available_detectors.best_for: Small to medium datasets where automatic threshold selection is valued
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is large or faster LOF-based methods are sufficient

available_detectors.name: LODA
weaknesses: Random projections may miss certain anomaly patterns
Sensitive to number of bins and cuts
available_detectors.best_for: Streaming or online anomaly detection with limited computational resources
available_detectors.avoid_when: Batch setting with enough time for more powerful methods

available_detectors.name: LOF
strengths: Adapts to varying densities across the dataset
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets with clusters of varying densities where local anomalies are of interest
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large (>50K) or data is uniformly distributed

available_detectors.name: LSCP
strengths: Locally selects the best detector for each region
weaknesses: Requires a list of pre-instantiated base detectors
Slower due to training multiple detectors
available_detectors.best_for: Scenarios where diverse base detectors are available and local performance varies
available_detectors.avoid_when: Only one detector type is appropriate or computational budget is limited

available_detectors.name: LUNAR
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n * k * d + n * h * epochs)
strengths: Learns to score anomalies from neighbor graphs via GNN
Combines neighborhood structure with learned representations
Supports both score and weight model types
weaknesses: More complex setup than classical methods
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets where learned neighborhood-based scoring outperforms handcrafted rules
available_detectors.avoid_when: PyTorch is not available or simpler KNN/LOF methods work well

available_detectors.name: MAD
strengths: Robust to outliers in the training data
available_detectors.best_for: Univariate outlier detection with a robust central tendency measure
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data is multivariate or relationships between features are important

available_detectors.name: MCD
strengths: Resistant to masking effects from outliers
weaknesses: Assumes data follows a Gaussian distribution
May fail in high-dimensional settings (d > n)
available_detectors.best_for: Multivariate Gaussian-like data requiring robust covariance estimation
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data is non-Gaussian, very high-dimensional, or strongly nonlinear

available_detectors.name: MO_GAAL
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(k * n * d * h * epochs) where k is number of generators
strengths: Multiple generators provide diverse outlier references
Better coverage of outlier space than SO_GAAL
weaknesses: Even more complex training than SO_GAAL
available_detectors.best_for: Complex datasets where diverse generated outlier references improve detection
available_detectors.avoid_when: Computational resources are limited or simpler GAN approaches suffice

available_detectors.name: OCSVM
strengths: Strong theoretical foundation from SVM literature
weaknesses: Cubic training time for large datasets
Sensitive to kernel and nu parameter choice
Does not scale well beyond ~10K samples
available_detectors.best_for: Medium-sized datasets where a flexible decision boundary is needed
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large or real-time training is required

available_detectors.name: PCA
strengths: Effective when anomalies lie in minor principal components
weaknesses: Sensitive to the number of components selected
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets with linear structure where outliers deviate from main variance directions
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data has strong nonlinear structure or outliers align with principal components

available_detectors.name: QMCD
strengths: Based on uniformity criterion from quasi-Monte Carlo theory
weaknesses: Assumes outliers deviate from uniform space-filling
available_detectors.best_for: Detecting anomalies as deviations from uniform space-filling in moderate-dimensional data
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large or high-dimensional

available_detectors.name: RGraph
strengths: Random walk on graph reveals connectivity anomalies
Tunable transition steps for multi-scale detection
weaknesses: Requires tuning of graph construction parameters
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets where graph connectivity and neighborhood structure reveal anomalies
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large or a simpler proximity method suffices

available_detectors.name: ROD
strengths: Considers rotations to detect outliers across projections
weaknesses: Designed primarily for 3D data, may not generalize well to very high dimensions
Limited theoretical analysis compared to classical methods
available_detectors.best_for: Low-dimensional data where rotation-invariant outlier detection is desired
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data is high-dimensional or a well-tuned alternative is available

available_detectors.name: SOD
strengths: Effective when anomalies hide in subspaces
Reference set approach captures local structure
weaknesses: Requires tuning of ref_set and n_neighbors
May miss anomalies not aligned with axis-parallel subspaces
available_detectors.best_for: High-dimensional data where outliers deviate in axis-parallel subspaces
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data is low-dimensional or anomalies require oblique subspaces to detect

available_detectors.name: SOS
strengths: Based on affinity and binding probability concepts
Perplexity parameter controls local vs global sensitivity
available_detectors.best_for: Medium-sized datasets where probability-calibrated outlier scores are valuable
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large (>10K samples) due to quadratic complexity

available_detectors.name: SO_GAAL
strengths: GAN-based approach generates informative outlier samples
Novel adversarial training framework for OD
weaknesses: Slow training compared to non-deep methods
available_detectors.best_for: Exploratory anomaly detection with GAN-generated reference outliers
available_detectors.avoid_when: Stable and fast results are required, or dataset is small

available_detectors.name: SUOD
strengths: Accelerates large-scale outlier detection via approximation
Supports parallel execution of base detectors
Modular framework for combining multiple detectors
weaknesses: Requires choosing and configuring base estimators
available_detectors.best_for: Large-scale datasets where running multiple detectors is desired but time is limited
available_detectors.avoid_when: Exact results from a single well-chosen detector are preferred

available_detectors.name: Sampling
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n * s * d) where s is subset size
weaknesses: Randomness from sampling can affect reproducibility
May miss local outliers with small subset sizes
available_detectors.best_for: Large-scale datasets requiring fast distance-based outlier detection
available_detectors.avoid_when: Precise and deterministic results are required or dataset is small enough for exact methods

available_detectors.name: VAE
weaknesses: More complex to train than standard autoencoder
KL divergence term may dominate loss
Requires careful balancing of loss components
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets where probabilistic reconstruction scoring and smooth latent spaces are beneficial
available_detectors.avoid_when: Simpler autoencoder or non-deep methods work well, or dataset is very small

available_detectors.name: XGBOD
strengths: Combines unsupervised representations with supervised XGBoost
High accuracy when labels are available
weaknesses: Training is more expensive than unsupervised methods
available_detectors.best_for: Semi-supervised settings where some labeled anomalies are available
available_detectors.avoid_when: No labeled data is available or a purely unsupervised approach is needed

available_detectors.name: IForest

strengths: Linear time complexity with efficient implementation

available_detectors.name: KNN
weaknesses: Sensitive to distance metric and k choice
available_detectors.best_for: General-purpose distance-based outlier detection on moderate-sized datasets

available_detectors.name: ECOD
strengths: Strong benchmark performance across diverse datasets
weaknesses: May struggle with strongly correlated features
Assumes outliers deviate in at least one marginal dimension
available_detectors.best_for: General-purpose outlier detection when speed and interpretability are priorities

available_detectors.name: COPOD

weaknesses: Assumes feature-wise independence for tail modeling

available_detectors.name: HBOS
available_detectors.best_for: Large-scale datasets where speed is critical and features are roughly independent
available_detectors.avoid_when: Outliers only manifest through feature interactions or correlations

available_detectors.name: ABOD
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n^2 * d) for fast, O(n^3 * d) for default
strengths: Not affected by distance concentration in high dimensions
weaknesses: Computationally expensive, especially in default mode
Sensitive to noise in low-dimensional data
Requires sufficient neighbors for angle variance estimation
available_detectors.best_for: High-dimensional datasets where distance-based methods suffer from curse of dimensionality
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large or low-dimensional where distance-based methods work well

available_detectors.name: AE1SVM

Combines representation learning with boundary detection
weaknesses: Requires tuning of both AE and SVM hyperparameters
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets benefiting from joint representation learning and one-class classification
available_detectors.avoid_when: Simpler pipeline of separate AE + SVM works well, or dataset is small

available_detectors.name: ALAD
strengths: Bi-directional GAN avoids slow iterative inference of AnoGAN
weaknesses: Still subject to GAN training challenges
available_detectors.best_for: Scenarios where GAN-based detection is desired but fast inference is needed
available_detectors.avoid_when: Simpler reconstruction-based deep methods suffice or dataset is small

available_detectors.name: ANOMALOUS
available_detectors.best_for: Small-to-medium attributed graphs where smoothness matters
available_detectors.avoid_when: Graph is very large or anomalies are purely structural

available_detectors.name: AnoGAN
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n * d * h * epochs) + O(n * iterations) for inference
strengths: GAN learns the normal data distribution
Anomaly scoring via reconstruction in latent space
weaknesses: Slow inference due to iterative latent optimization
available_detectors.best_for: Complex data distributions where GAN-based generation quality is high
available_detectors.avoid_when: Fast inference is needed or training instability is a concern

available_detectors.name: AnomalyDAE
available_detectors.best_for: Attributed graphs where attention over neighbors reveals anomaly patterns
available_detectors.avoid_when: Graph is very large or structure is unimportant

available_detectors.name: AutoEncoder
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n * d * h * epochs) where h is hidden size
strengths: Reconstruction error is an intuitive anomaly score
weaknesses: Requires tuning of architecture and hyperparameters
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets with complex nonlinear structure where reconstruction-based scoring is appropriate
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is small, tabular and simple methods suffice, or training time is limited

available_detectors.name: CBLOF

Effective when data has clear cluster structure
weaknesses: Depends on quality of underlying clustering
Sensitive to number of clusters parameter

available_detectors.best_for: Data with well-separated clusters where outliers deviate from cluster structure
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data has no meaningful cluster structure or clusters are heavily overlapping

available_detectors.name: CD
strengths: Based on classical influence measures from regression
Interpretable as influence on regression fit
Works well when a regression model is appropriate
weaknesses: Not suitable for purely unsupervised settings without a model
available_detectors.best_for: Identifying influential observations in regression settings
available_detectors.avoid_when: No natural target variable exists or data is purely unsupervised

available_detectors.name: COF

weaknesses: Marginal improvement over LOF in many cases
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets where outliers lie along sparse connectivity paths between clusters
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is large or simpler methods like LOF already perform well

available_detectors.name: CONAD
weaknesses: Augmentation ratio is a sensitive hyperparameter
available_detectors.best_for: Attributed graphs where robustness to noise is important
available_detectors.avoid_when: Graph structure is too sparse for meaningful augmentation

available_detectors.name: CoLA
available_detectors.best_for: Attributed graphs where anomalies have unusual local neighborhoods
available_detectors.avoid_when: Graph is disconnected or has no node features

available_detectors.name: DIF

weaknesses: More computationally expensive than standard IForest
available_detectors.best_for: Complex datasets where standard Isolation Forest misses anomalies due to axis-aligned splits
available_detectors.avoid_when: Standard Isolation Forest performs well or dataset is small and simple

available_detectors.name: DOMINANT
available_detectors.best_for: Attributed graphs where anomalies manifest in both structure and attributes
available_detectors.avoid_when: Graph is very large (>10k nodes) or has no node features

available_detectors.name: DeepSVDD
strengths: Learns a compact hypersphere around normal data
Combines deep learning with SVDD objective
available_detectors.best_for: One-class anomaly detection where a compact normal data description is desired
available_detectors.avoid_when: Normal data is multi-modal or simpler one-class methods are sufficient

available_detectors.name: DevNet
strengths: Can leverage a few labeled anomalies (semi-supervised)
Deviation loss directly optimizes anomaly scores
weaknesses: Requires at least a few labeled anomalies for best results
Sensitive to architecture and loss parameters
available_detectors.best_for: Semi-supervised anomaly detection where a small number of labeled anomalies are available
available_detectors.avoid_when: No labeled anomalies are available or dataset is too small for deep learning

available_detectors.name: EmbeddingOD
strengths: Leverages foundation model embeddings for anomaly detection
Supports text and image data natively
weaknesses: Embedding quality depends on the foundation model
Higher memory usage for large embedding dimensions
available_detectors.best_for: Anomaly detection on unstructured data (text, images) via foundation model representations
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data is already tabular or a suitable encoder is not available

available_detectors.name: FeatureBagging
weaknesses: Performance depends on choice of base detector
Slower than single detector due to ensemble overhead
May not improve over base if features are all relevant
available_detectors.best_for: High-dimensional data with potentially irrelevant features
available_detectors.avoid_when: All features are relevant or a single strong detector suffices

available_detectors.name: GMM
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n * k * d^2) per EM iteration
weaknesses: Sensitive to initialization and number of components
EM convergence not guaranteed to global optimum
available_detectors.best_for: Data with multi-modal distributions that can be approximated by Gaussian mixtures
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data does not follow mixture-of-Gaussians assumption or is very high-dimensional

available_detectors.name: GUIDE
weaknesses: Sparse graphs may have few triangles
available_detectors.best_for: Dense attributed graphs with meaningful higher-order structures
available_detectors.avoid_when: Graph is tree-like (no triangles) or very large

available_detectors.name: HDBSCAN
strengths: Automatically finds clusters of varying density
Identifies noise points as potential outliers
weaknesses: May be slow for very large datasets
Outlier scores derived from cluster membership
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets with variable-density clusters where noise points are outliers
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data does not have cluster structure or very high-dimensional

available_detectors.name: INNE
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n * t * s) where t is n_estimators, s is sample size
strengths: Handles local anomalies better than Isolation Forest
weaknesses: Requires tuning of sample size and number of estimators
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets where local density variations matter and Isolation Forest underperforms
available_detectors.avoid_when: A simpler method like IForest already works well

available_detectors.name: KDE
weaknesses: Sensitive to bandwidth and kernel selection
available_detectors.best_for: Low-to-moderate dimensional data where non-parametric density estimation is desired
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data is high-dimensional or dataset is very large

available_detectors.name: KPCA
strengths: Captures nonlinear relationships via kernel trick
Extension of PCA to nonlinear manifolds
available_detectors.best_for: Moderately sized datasets with nonlinear structure
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large due to quadratic kernel matrix or a linear model suffices

available_detectors.name: KShape
available_detectors.best_for: Detecting shape-based anomalies in short-to-medium time series subsequences
available_detectors.avoid_when: Time series is very long (performance degrades)

available_detectors.name: LMDD
strengths: Multiple deviation measures available (AAD, IQR, MAD)
weaknesses: Results can vary due to random projections
Requires tuning of number of iterations and measure
May underperform with nonlinear anomaly patterns
available_detectors.best_for: Multivariate data where anomalies are detectable through linear projections
available_detectors.avoid_when: Anomalies require nonlinear feature combinations to detect

available_detectors.name: LOCI
strengths: Multi-granularity outlier detection via alpha parameter

weaknesses: Difficult to scale to large datasets
available_detectors.best_for: Small to medium datasets where automatic threshold selection is valued
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is large or faster LOF-based methods are sufficient

available_detectors.name: LODA
weaknesses: Random projections may miss certain anomaly patterns
Sensitive to number of bins and cuts
available_detectors.best_for: Streaming or online anomaly detection with limited computational resources
available_detectors.avoid_when: Batch setting with enough time for more powerful methods

available_detectors.name: LOF
strengths: Adapts to varying densities across the dataset
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets with clusters of varying densities where local anomalies are of interest
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large (>50K) or data is uniformly distributed

available_detectors.name: LSCP
strengths: Locally selects the best detector for each region
weaknesses: Requires a list of pre-instantiated base detectors
Slower due to training multiple detectors
available_detectors.best_for: Scenarios where diverse base detectors are available and local performance varies
available_detectors.avoid_when: Only one detector type is appropriate or computational budget is limited

available_detectors.name: LSTMAD
available_detectors.best_for: Multivariate and long time series with complex temporal patterns
available_detectors.avoid_when: Fast inference is critical or data is very short

available_detectors.name: LUNAR
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(n * k * d + n * h * epochs)
strengths: Learns to score anomalies from neighbor graphs via GNN
Combines neighborhood structure with learned representations
Supports both score and weight model types
weaknesses: More complex setup than classical methods
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets where learned neighborhood-based scoring outperforms handcrafted rules
available_detectors.avoid_when: PyTorch is not available or simpler KNN/LOF methods work well

available_detectors.name: MAD
strengths: Robust to outliers in the training data
available_detectors.best_for: Univariate outlier detection with a robust central tendency measure
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data is multivariate or relationships between features are important

available_detectors.name: MCD
strengths: Resistant to masking effects from outliers
weaknesses: Assumes data follows a Gaussian distribution
May fail in high-dimensional settings (d > n)
available_detectors.best_for: Multivariate Gaussian-like data requiring robust covariance estimation
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data is non-Gaussian, very high-dimensional, or strongly nonlinear

available_detectors.name: MO_GAAL
available_detectors.complexity_time: O(k * n * d * h * epochs) where k is number of generators
strengths: Multiple generators provide diverse outlier references

weaknesses: Even more complex training than SO_GAAL
available_detectors.best_for: Complex datasets where diverse generated outlier references improve detection
available_detectors.avoid_when: Computational resources are limited or simpler GAN approaches suffice

available_detectors.name: MatrixProfile
weaknesses: O(n^2) may be slow on long series
available_detectors.best_for: Subsequence anomaly detection where exact distances matter
available_detectors.avoid_when: Out-of-sample prediction is needed

available_detectors.name: MultiModalOD

weaknesses: Higher computational cost with multiple modalities
available_detectors.best_for: Anomaly detection on multi-modal data combining text, image, or other modalities

weaknesses: Sensitive to the number of components selected
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets with linear structure where outliers deviate from main variance directions
available_detectors.avoid_when: Data has strong nonlinear structure or outliers align with principal components

available_detectors.name: QMCD
strengths: Based on uniformity criterion from quasi-Monte Carlo theory
weaknesses: Assumes outliers deviate from uniform space-filling

available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large or high-dimensional

strengths: Random walk on graph reveals connectivity anomalies
Tunable transition steps for multi-scale detection
weaknesses: Requires tuning of graph construction parameters
available_detectors.best_for: Datasets where graph connectivity and neighborhood structure reveal anomalies
available_detectors.avoid_when: Dataset is very large or a simpler proximity method suffices

available_detectors.avoid_when: Node attributes are available and important for anomaly detection
